FL-2026-HB1245.s: The bill would limit how much bulk Class AA biosolids fertilizer and compost could be spread on land to the proper agronomic rate, which is the amount plants can use safely. It would also require some site owners or operators to keep application records and give them to the state environmental agency if asked. The University of Florida would have to publish recommended rates for reusing these products, and some of them could not be sold or given out for farm use unless set rules are met. It was vetoed by the governor.

FL-2026-HB1285.s: The bill would bar Florida’s environmental agency from issuing or renewing some permits for spreading biosolids on land if a nearby wastewater plant takes septage and meets set rules. It affects certain biosolids land application sites and wastewater treatment facilities, and it was approved by the Governor on June 25, 2026.

FL-2026-HB1329.s: Florida counties would have to post tentative and final budgets on their websites for new time periods. Counties would also have to hold a budget workshop by a set date, post a budget reduction exercise or a link to it, and share budget planning calendars online. The bill became law.

FL-2026-HB1389.s: The law changes local rules for some housing projects. Counties and cities must allow certain multifamily and mixed-use housing on some property, and they cannot use some height limits, setbacks, or stepbacks to block those projects. It also lets some applicants update their plans and allows local governments to give a density bonus, which means extra building rights, to landowners who donate land for affordable housing for military families. The law also orders a study on mezzanine finance and tiny homes for certain uses.

FL-2026-HB1405.s: The bill creates a statewide project for finding missing people with special needs through centers for autism and related disabilities. It says people for the project would be chosen based on set criteria. It includes a $1,000,000 appropriation and was approved by the governor.

FL-2026-HB145.s: Raises the dollar caps on when people can sue the state, its agencies, and local government bodies over tort claims, which are harm claims. It also changes some rules for starting these cases and for when a claim is treated as denied if no final answer is given. It would also change the time limit for filing these claims and some exceptions to that rule.

FL-2026-HB175.s: Payment stablecoins, which are digital coins used for payments, would be added to Florida’s money-laundering rules for money services businesses. The bill would require some stablecoin issuers to follow state rules, get a license or qualify for an exception, and give notice to the state banking office in some cases. It also says some stablecoin transactions are not covered by certain state rules and that some stablecoins are not securities. The bill became law in 2026.

FL-2026-HB253.s: The bill changes the purpose of Florida’s Veterans Dental Care Grant Program. It applies to veterans and became law after the governor approved it.

FL-2026-HB325.s: The bill would let Florida use some workforce development money for more than just construction jobs, including grants to private schools for certain training and certification programs. It would also let some inmates join programs to earn certain commercial driver licenses and other job credentials, if they qualify. The Department of Corrections would have to send a yearly report, and a trained correctional officer would need to be present during certain inmate transport or vehicle use. The bill passed the legislature but was vetoed by the governor.

FL-2026-HB33.s: The law gives honorary names to certain transportation facilities in some counties and tells the state transportation department to put up signs. It affects those local roads or other transportation sites in the listed counties. It was approved by the governor on July 1, 2026.

FL-2026-HB359.s: The bill changes rules for search warrants in Florida. It would let warrants be used to recover a body, set new time limits for returning warrants and for using warrants on certain devices, and allow police to review data on those devices after set periods if they were seized on time. It would also let judges allow remote appearances for warrant requests and let police seek a warrant to use a drone in some cases. It was approved by the governor and became law.

FL-2026-HB4003.s: The measure changes how vacancies on the Marco Island city council are filled. It would require a special election to fill a vacancy when the council passes a resolution, with an exception for vacancies that happen within 1 year before a general election. It also changes when the Governor must fill vacancies, lets the Governor call a special election in some cases, and requires a referendum.

FL-2026-HB4005.s: The law changes how the City of Naples Airport Authority in Collier County is run. It switches authority members from being appointed to being elected and sets rules for those elections, member terms, and qualifications. It also changes the rules for who may serve, pay for members, and how temporary service and vacancies are handled.

FL-2026-HB4007.s: The law requires the Martin County Board of County Commissioners to set up a process, by local rule, for sending money from the County Health Care Fund to all licensed hospitals in the county. It also sets rules for who counts as an indigent resident, meaning a low-income resident, for county payments for hospital care. The law removes the County Health Care Review Board provisions.

FL-2026-HB4013.s: Lawmakers changed the boundaries of the Iona-McGregor Fire Protection & Rescue Service District and removed old laws tied to the Fort Myers Beach Fire Control District. The measure merges the two districts, shifts the governing body during the change, and moves the Fort Myers Beach district’s assets and debts to the Iona-McGregor district. It also requires a referendum, which is a public vote.

FL-2026-HB4019.s: In Lake County, the bill would limit when health care providers, trauma centers, and emergency transport services can be paid for treating people in the county detention center if they do not already have a contract with the county. It applies to care and transport for inmates housed in that jail. The bill was approved by the Governor and became law.

FL-2026-HB4025.s: The measure transfers certain state-owned land and the buildings on it from the Board of Trustees of the Internal Improvement Trust Fund to the Village Council of the Village of Tequesta. It also sets rules for how the land must be used, owned, sold, or otherwise handled, and calls for the transfer to happen by a set date. The bill became law.

FL-2026-HB4027.s: The law changes Hillsborough County Public Schools so the school superintendent would be elected instead of appointed. It also requires a local vote, called a referendum, on that change. The bill became law.

FL-2026-HB4029.s: Changes the Hillsborough County charter by changing the number of county commissioners and the boundaries of county districts. It also changes how districts are redrawn, how some county votes are counted, and how charter review board members are chosen and charter changes are proposed. The bill also sets rules for moving to single-member districts and an 11-member board, and it was approved by the governor.

FL-2026-HB4033.s: The law changes the definitions of “family day care home” and “large family child care home” in Palm Beach County to set the highest number of children that can be cared for in these homes. It affects child care homes in that county and became law on July 1, 2026.

FL-2026-HB4037.s: Changes how the Pasco County Mosquito Control District is run. It would revise term limits for members of the district board and require the Pasco County Board of County Commissioners to label geographic districts with set numbers. It would also set rules for a certain subdistrict.

FL-2026-HB4041.s: This law sets payment rules for health care services for inmates at the Indian River County detention center. It limits when a health care provider, a hospital, or an emergency medical transport service can be paid if they do not have a county contract. It applies in Indian River County.

FL-2026-HB4045.s: The measure would make the Jacksonville Aviation Authority responsible for helping develop Cecil Airport as a center for aerospace and related businesses. It would also require the authority to present a yearly economic development plan for Cecil Airport to the Jacksonville City Council for review. The bill would change the dollar limits for some purchases made by the authority. It became law.

FL-2026-HB4049.s: The bill would let the Duval County School Board hire its own general counsel, or chief legal adviser, who would be separate from the City of Jacksonville’s legal office. Some legal services would still be handled through the city’s general counsel office, and the measure became law.

FL-2026-HB4053.s: Changes the fire district’s extra property charges in Avalon Beach-Mulat in Santa Rosa County. It would exempt churches and certain religious groups from those charges if they already do not pay regular property tax. It would also change how the district figures those charges for homes and for industrial properties over 40,000 square feet.

FL-2026-HB4057.s: The law transfers certain state-owned land in DeFuniak Springs to the city council of DeFuniak Springs in Walton County. It gives a description of the property and sets rules for how it may be used, sold, or otherwise handled. The property must be conveyed by a set date. It was approved by the Governor and became chapter law on July 1, 2026.

FL-2026-HB4061.s: Creates a new special district in Hillsborough County called the Land Reserve Stewardship District. It sets up the district’s boundaries, board, manager, money rules, and powers to plan and pay for roads, utilities, and other community services inside the district. It also covers bonds, taxes and assessments, district changes or ending, notice to homebuyers, and a vote on the measure.

FL-2026-HB4063.s: Changes the rules for the West Palm Beach Police Pension Fund. It would update who can join, when officers can retire, how retirement pay is figured, and the choices for getting benefits. It also affects death benefits, investment rules, small lump-sum payments, rollovers from other plans, and what happens if someone goes back to work after retirement. It became law in Florida as Chapter 2026-213.

FL-2026-HB4067.s: This law makes the Plantation Acres Improvement District in Broward County part of the City of Plantation as a dependent district. The city council and mayor take over as the district’s board, and the district’s assets, debts, contracts, rules, and policies stay in place until the city changes them. It also sets a transition process, ends the district as an independent special district, and requires a vote by the people in the district.

FL-2026-HB4075.s: The bill would let a sign be placed on certain agriculturally zoned property in the Town of Davie, Broward County, as an exception to state law. It passed the legislature but was vetoed by the Governor.

FL-2026-HB4079.s: Creates the Uplands Steward District in Marion County and sets its boundaries and powers. It also sets up district leaders, money rules, and plans for bonds, loans, taxes, and special assessments. The bill became law on July 1, 2026.

FL-2026-HB4081.s: The law changes the Eastpoint Water and Sewer District in Franklin County by adding more land to its boundaries. It also gives the district board more powers and sets up votes by local residents, called referenda, on some changes. The law also includes rules for how it is to be carried out.

FL-2026-HB4091.s: Creates the University Town Center Improvement District as a special taxing district in Sarasota and Manatee counties. It sets the district's boundaries, powers, and board rules, and allows landowner meetings, special assessments, and bonds. The bill was approved by the governor and became chapter 2026-222 on July 1, 2026.

FL-2026-HB4095.s: Creates the Headwaters Water Control District in Indian River County as a public corporation and sets out its charter, boundaries, and basic rules. It also covers the care and use of certain canals and how the district’s charter can be changed. The bill became law.

FL-2026-HB4103.s: Creates a water and sewer district for Apalachicola in Franklin County and sets up its board, powers, and boundaries. It affects the City of Apalachicola, the new district, and people who use local water and sewer service. The law also sets a process to transfer service, assets, debts, contracts, and some employee roles to the district.

FL-2026-HB4105.s: This law expands the Port St. Joe Port Authority to include Franklin, Gadsden, and Liberty counties. It also changes who serves on the authority’s governing board and sets up a transition with staggered terms, so members start and end service at different times. It affects the port authority and the counties named in the law.

FL-2026-HB461.s: High school students who volunteer to help poll workers would be exempt from rules that bar certain agencies and local officials from using private money or some personal services for election costs. It applies to election work at polling places. The measure was vetoed by the Governor.

FL-2026-HB47.s: Changes the rules for child protective investigations when a report involves a specific medical diagnosis. It would let the Department of Children and Families wait to send some allegations to law enforcement until its investigation is done, and it would require child protection teams to work with a licensed doctor or advanced practice nurse with the right experience in some cases. The bill also requires the investigator to tell the person under investigation about a duty, and for the medical professional to send a written report within a set time.

FL-2026-HB505.s: The law changes rules for virtual currency kiosks and the businesses that run them in Florida. It says these businesses must register or renew their registration, give certain notices and information to the state office, show customer warnings at the kiosk, give a receipt after each transaction, and give a full refund in some cases. It also changes when money services businesses and related parties can face discipline and says some money transmitters are exempt from kiosk registration but still follow certain rules.

FL-2026-HB6509.s: This law provides $1.2 million to compensate the Estate of Mark LaGatta for injuries and damages from an accident involving the Department of Transportation. It says the money paid under this law and under Florida law are the only compensation for claims from the incident. It also limits attorney fees for this claim to 25 percent of the amount awarded.

FL-2026-HB6515.s: The bill provides money to compensate Lourdes Latour and Edward Latour for injuries they say were caused by Miami-Dade County’s negligence. It sets a $500,000 claim limit and includes payment for attorney fees. It was approved by the governor and became law in 2026.

FL-2026-HB6517.s: The bill sets aside $2.3 million to pay Heriberto A. Sanchez-Mayen for injuries he says came from negligence by the City of St. Petersburg. It also limits how much can be paid and covers attorney fees. The measure was approved by the Governor and became Chapter 2026-228.

FL-2026-HB755.s: The bill would let certain groups skip some payment and performance bond rules, which are promises to pay for work if a contractor does not finish. It would also extend certain Florida Forever land-buying funds so they can be used to buy land in the Florida Keys area. The bill was approved by the governor and became law.

FL-2026-HB797.s: The law updates rules for nonprofit corporations in Florida and makes them line up more closely with standard business law language. It changes how nonprofits handle members, board seats, meetings, voting, mergers, and written notice, and it adds rules for officers and directors to act in good faith and with reasonable care. It also gives certain officers and directors liability immunity and adds rules for property kept for charitable use.

FL-2026-HB893.s: The bill would let banks and other financial institutions hold money in certain trust accounts for uses allowed by a Florida Supreme Court rule. It would require some groups to use the interest and dividends from those accounts for set purposes. It was passed by lawmakers but later vetoed by the governor.

FL-2026-HB967.s: Local governments in Florida would have to accept certain kinds of payments, including payments made online. The bill affects units of local government that take payments from the public. It was approved by the Governor and became chapter 2026-169.

FL-2026-SB110.s: The bill changes when a person can be treated as owning certain property for a homestead tax exemption, which is a property tax break for a main home. It affects people seeking that exemption in Florida.

FL-2026-SB1180.s: The bill changes rules for community development districts. It says some synthetic turf rules do not apply when these districts enforce deed restrictions, which are private rules for homes or land. It also lets certain district board members be removed by recall and sets rules for how that recall vote works. The bill became law.

FL-2026-SB1332.s: Creates a special driver license or ID mark for certain career offenders. It would require them to report to the state motor vehicle agency in a set month to get an updated or renewed card, and some must do this within a set time after release. It would also let the agency share some images with law enforcement for public notice.

FL-2026-SB1452.s: The law changes several Department of Financial Services rules on reports, payroll timing, and public fund chart-of-accounts reporting. It also changes who can qualify for a hurricane mitigation inspection under the My Safe Florida Home Program, treats cash redemptions and debit card redemptions the same, and updates when certain business interests are considered abandoned. It also ratifies some rules about legal tender.

FL-2026-SB156.s: The bill would change Florida rules on crimes against law enforcement officers and some other public workers. It would change when people can use force to resist arrest or detention, increase punishment for manslaughter in some cases, and update rules for assault, battery, and resisting an officer. It became law in 2026.

FL-2026-SB1568.s: The law creates a Florida Stablecoin Pilot Program in the Department of Financial Services. It lets the department accept payment stablecoins and review the companies that issue them through checks, audits, and investigations. The department must also track the pilot program and collect certain data.

FL-2026-SB168.s: This law changes the list of places that can be named a public nuisance to include the site of a gambling house. It also changes how fines for public nuisances are billed and collected. The law removes a cap on the total fines that can be placed on a public nuisance.

FL-2026-SB382.s: Sets rules for riding electric bicycles and says they cannot be operated above a certain speed in some cases. It also would create a Micromobility Device Safety Task Force in the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles and require the Florida Highway Patrol, police departments, and sheriffs’ offices to keep a certain list starting on a set date. The bill was vetoed by the Governor.

FL-2026-SB436.s: The bill changes who is counted as a "prison releasee reoffender," which means someone who may face tougher punishment after release from prison. It adds people who commit or try to commit battery on a law enforcement officer and cause bodily injury. It also raises criminal penalties for a second or later battery after a prior conviction for resisting an officer with violence.

FL-2026-SB594.s: Counties and eligible cities in Florida would be allowed to use some housing aid money for lot rent help for mobile home owners for a set time. Their local housing plans would also have to include certain strategies, and they could give money for home repairs or emergency repairs for mobile home owners. The bill passed and was approved by the Governor.

FL-2026-SB628.s: The measure gives honorary names to certain transportation facilities in some counties and one city. It also tells the state Transportation Department to put up signs and changes the name of one interchange. It became law.

FL-2026-SB688.s: The bill would create a Board of Naturopathic Medicine in the Department of Health and set rules for naturopathic doctors. It would bar people without a license from practicing naturopathic medicine or using certain job titles or short forms. It would also set ways to get a license by exam or by holding a license from another place, and it would change continuing education rules for naturopathic doctors. It was vetoed by the Governor.

FL-2026-SB7004.s: The bill would keep in place a public records exemption for certain conviction integrity unit reinvestigation information. It affects records used when a unit reviews a criminal conviction again, and it was approved by the Governor and became law.

FL-2026-SB7014.s: The bill would extend a public records exemption for certain information gathered in investigations into social media platform activities. It affects records held by the Attorney General, the Department of Legal Affairs, and law enforcement agencies, and it became law on June 16, 2026.

FL-2026-SB7040.s: Creates the Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund in the Governor’s office. It would set rules for money in the fund, including putting federal reimbursements for state emergency costs in a separate account. The fund could not be used to buy aircraft, boats, or motor vehicles.

FL-2026-SB962.s: This law revises some land-use category definitions used for residential development. It would exclude farms, farm operations, and related uses from those categories. It affects local land-use rules and residential building decisions.

FL-2026F-SB4F.s: Changes how Florida property tax rules are defined and applied for counties and cities. It also changes limits on the highest tax rate some local governments may charge. The bill was approved by the governor and became law.

FL-2027-SB12.s: Miami-Dade County would be required to pay money to Odalys Fortes, Pablo Becerra, and Aliyah Isabel Mieryteran for injuries tied to the county’s negligence. It also sets limits on the compensation and on lawyer fees.

FL-2027-SB14.s: The bill would provide money from Miami-Dade County to compensate the estate of Juan Carlos Martinez Silva for his death, which the summary says was caused by a county police officer’s negligence. It also sets limits on the compensation and on payment of lawyer fees. The claim amount is $2,761,767.

FL-2027-SB16.s: Would provide relief to L.P., a minor, by the Florida Department of Children and Families. It would give money to compensate L.P. for injuries and other losses tied to the actions of department employees and caseworkers. The bill includes an appropriation of $28,000,000 and sets limits on compensation and on fees and costs.

FL-2027-SB18.s: Would provide payment to the estate of James Corpora from Miami-Dade County to settle a claim tied to his death in a bus crash. The bill sets the claim amount at $1,050,000 and includes payment of attorney fees. It affects the estate and Miami-Dade County.

FL-2027-SB20.s: Would provide money to compensate former Broward County Sheriff’s Deputy Maury Hernandez for injuries and losses tied to the Department of Corrections’ failure to enforce probation rules. It also says some liens, which are legal claims on money, would be waived. The bill sets a $5,000,000 appropriation and includes limits on compensation and attorney fees.

FL-2027-SB22.s: This bill would provide relief to Michael Barnett, both for himself and as the parent and guardian of R.B. It would set aside $296,400 to pay for injuries and damages linked to the Department of Children and Families. It would also set limits on the amount paid and on attorney fees.

FL-2027-SB24.s: Provides money to compensate C.C. for injuries and damage blamed on the Department of Children and Families. The bill sets aside $20,000,000 and also limits how much can be paid for compensation, lawyer fees, and some costs.

FL-2027-SB26.s: The bill would provide money from Miami-Dade County to the estate of Oscar Cabrera and Stephanie Cabrera to cover damages tied to Mr. Cabrera’s wrongful death. It would set a limit on the payment, including attorney fees. The claim amount is $4,024,441.

FL-2027-SB28.s: The bill would provide relief for Maximus Giannikos by the City of Clearwater. It would set up an appropriation, or public payment, to compensate him for injuries said to have been caused by the city’s negligence. It would also limit the amount of compensation and attorney fees.

FL-2027-SB30.s: The bill would provide relief to the estate of Lisa-Maria Carter through the University of South Florida. It would set aside money to compensate the estate for injuries and damages tied to care by doctors employed by the university board. The claim amount is $850,000, and it would also set limits on compensation and attorney fees.

FL-2027-SB32.s: This bill would set up payments from the City of Temple Terrace to compensate Samantha Sakowski, Li. S., and B.J. for injuries, and the estate of Le. S. for death, tied to a claim that says the city was negligent. It would cover a claim amount of $22,300,000. It also sets limits on how much can be paid for the compensation and attorney fees.

FL-2027-SB34.s: This bill would require the Broward County Sheriff’s Office to pay the Estate of M.N. $2.5 million. The money is meant to compensate the estate for injuries and damages tied to M.N.’s death after the office’s negligence. It also says this payment and the amount already paid under Florida law are the sole compensation for claims from this situation, and attorney fees may not exceed 25 percent of the amount awarded.

FL-2027-SB36.s: Would provide money to compensate Krystle Mace and Leonard Mace for injuries they say were caused by Charlotte County's negligence. It also sets limits on the compensation and on attorney fees. The claim amount is $6,080,263.

FL-2027-SB38.s: The bill would provide payment to Elijah Brinson through the Public Health Trust of Miami-Dade County, which does business as Jackson Memorial Hospital. It would set aside money to compensate him for injuries tied to the negligence of trust employees. It would also limit how much could be paid for compensation and attorney fees.

FL-2027-SB40.s: The bill would provide relief for H.H. by the Department of Children and Families and set aside money to pay for injuries and damages tied to the department’s negligence. It would provide $14,926,640 in compensation and set limits on that payment and on some fees and costs.

FL-2027-SB42.s: The bill would provide relief for Eugene Wyatt and set aside money to compensate him for injuries and losses linked to his confinement at the Arthur G. Dozier School for Boys, if certain conditions are met. It would limit the amount of compensation and the payment of attorney fees, and the appropriation is $21,254.

FL-2027-SB44.s: The bill would provide payment to Sean Hurley for injuries linked to the Orange County Sheriff’s Office. It would set aside $20,721,629 for that claim and place limits on the compensation and attorney fees.
